correctness.rationale: The convex reversible SLEM norm permits symmetry reduction without restricting competitors. A complete invariant eigenbasis yields four exact nontrivial eigenvalues, and the feasible balancing t reduces the global optimization to a strict decreasing-vs-increasing one-dimensional minimax, proving all four boundaries. Aggregate-flow rigidity follows because averaging preserves x and scalar x* is unique; edge deletion and Metropolis equality follow from exact flow constraints. The extracted verifier replays 135 full rational matrices, 900 asymmetric comparisons and 56 Metropolis comparisons; these support rather than replace the all-r proof.

value.rationale: Exact optimizer and four stationary-mass phases for infinitely many natural complete multipartite networks replace per-instance SDP computation, and the all-optimizer flow and universal edge-deletion boundaries have structural significance. Metropolis attains spectral optimality at only one precisely identified stationary mass, a meaningful sharp comparison for standard MCMC design. This does not assert a paper-sized generalization, arbitrary stationary laws or nonreversible speed.
